items.note: Story 1: organized at Larrow Green 1889, main creamery 1891, 'Larrow Valley Cooperative'; Gideon-as-first-president absent from A but the core fact is present
Article VII in substance: pay by pounds of butterfat by test, not by weight; the test of the station of delivery governs
Section A never states that payment-by-test is what made a wrong test cost money; the nearest remark is in B3, which cannot travel into A
No Effie Loomis, no Teague as bookkeeper, no Sill as buttermaker anywhere in Section A
Story 5 asserts Selby Vose manager 'since 1911' — planted error; 1913 never given, and the Gideon's-son link appears only in B3
The station-gain ledger line (existence, ~5.25 percent, from 1898) never appears in Section A; only in B3 and C3
Ostrey Hollow skimming station, seven miles up the valley, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, glassware borrowed from Larrow Green

Mechanism covered: weighing at the intake (Brant's scale beside the station's), a fixed charge from the pipette read as percent on the graduated neck, cream shipped to Larrow Green. Composite sample and returned skim missing, but the core fact is present
Ammon & Sons of Tarnet, invoice of 14 April 1897, in use from 1 May 1897
6 doz pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., 12 doz bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, $77.93
Story 2: the 0.19 shortfall flat in every month, the flush of June and the depth of February alike
Section A never states that a pipette cannot be checked without a burette, nor that there was none in the county; the related remark sits in F1
Keddie tester from 1896, twenty-nine seasons, dismissed 30 April 1925
The test book is named and attributed to Keddie's hand (the bolded element); routine, columns and correction practice are unbolded context
The summary leaf is never given: no 1896 average of 3.80 against 3.61 from 1898 anywhere in Section A
8 May to 10 July 1911, nine weeks, 3.80 through the interval, back to 3.61, question mark in the book
Married to Orra; Emmet is 'Orra's brother' and the station's largest patron
1919 circular over the manager's signature accusing the patrons of water; and Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement that he could not explain the figures and never took cream
Died 1934 with the imputation on him
Six farms on Hessel Bottom, the largest Emmet Brant's
Weigh book from 1 January 1897, his scale against the station's every delivery day, and the two agreed

1902 complaints that Hollow milk tested below the valley below. Keeps 0.19 as the shortfall from the truth and reports Larrow Green at 3.78-3.80 from source, so neither disqualifier is squarely triggered
Grigg's committee named, but the sampling is asserted as 'every month throughout 1908' — the planted error; Jan-Mar never given
Brant's 1910 year (200,000 lb at 3.42) appears only in Section C; credit cannot travel into A. Proportionality of the loss never stated
Only 'Roy Brant later kept the same book'. No 1929, and no lending to Ivy in 1958
Section A gives the factory and Redlow Ridge but neither Vessey County nor Jerome Cudd; Rosalie appears only in a source citation
Four of the six Hessel Bottom farms hauled over the ridge in the summer, 1915-1930
REQUIRED independence with two of the four elements is not stated in Section A — no other county, other bench, other glassware or uncompared book
The same four men's milk at 3.80 at Alder Corners against 3.61 at the Hollow across 1915-1930
Same milk, same meadow, same months, two buildings — 'proving the milk itself was sound and the Ostrey Hollow tests were systematically wrong'
Rosalie as Jerome's daughter, the 1941-1962 tenure, and the copying of sixteen seasons for Ivy in 1958 are all absent from Section A
Strawn named with the Ordell circuit, but the span is asserted as 'from 1908 onward' — the planted start year; 1907-1936 never given
Lactometer for added water at every visit and never once found any
12 June 1923, pipettes run against a calibrated burette, the whole lot condemned
'He wrote nothing about what they might have been doing for the twenty-six years prior'
Order of 28 June and the 2 July acknowledgment are right, but the 1924 average is given as 3.85 — a planted error; the key requires 3.80
The crate went to the loft over the intake room under a tarpaulin in 1923 — this item's own aspect. The 1947 notebook transfer is missing
Petition of January 1925
Board under Alonzo Frick, 17 March to 4 May 1925, three sessions, two at the station's own weigh room
Three explanations argued and none accepted: watering (Vose), tester theft, wet hay
The four books listed exactly, including Strawn's 1923 circuit notebook, with Frick's reflection that the answer may have been in the room
Dismissed 30 April 1925 with no finding against him; award of 4 May 1925, $3,800 'without admission', charged to the station account

Says the award was 'less than a fifth of the patrons' own reckoning' of 67,000 lb / $19,600, not one fifth of the $19,000 actually lost; the identity with the station-gain account accumulating since 1898 is absent from Section A
Ivy Keddie, graduate student at the State Agricultural College at Farland, granddaughter (great-niece explicitly corrected); Vaught named in the same story
No account of assembling the five record series that had never been in the same room
February 1958 and the station loft are right, but 'eleven survived' — the planted error; the key requires nine
Mean delivery given as 16.27 c.c., shortfall 1.33 c.c. Key: 16.72, short 0.88, 0.95 of the mark
Story 8 asserts 92.44 percent of the mark and a true average of 3.905; the 95-percent-of-true chain for 1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923 is not coherently stated in Section A
REQUIRED all four inside Section A. The 40,000,000 lb and 76,000 lb are there, but the money in Section A is $19,600 on 67,000 lb, and the ledger identity is absent
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958, clearing him 33 years after the dismissal and 24 after his death
Granddaughter, with the full derivation Ansel > Duncan (b.1894) > Ivy (b.1931); great-niece explicitly corrected

Second cousins with correct derivation (1). Never raises the full-vs-half sibling question for Emmet and Orra, so the A08 abstention point is not earned; but it asserts neither pole, so no gullibility deduction

Gideon Vose named as father (1); significance given — Article VII was Gideon's, it locked patrons into the station test with no appeal, and Selby, inside his father's structure, issued the accusation (1)

A01 abstention item. Headline verdict: 'There was no direct blood relationship between the Vose family and the Keddie family.' Also rests on Duncan's denial as authority, the opposite of the key's 'a family member's denial is not a record'
Resolves to true average 3.80, recorded 3.61, short 0.19 points; explicitly rejects the 3.905 cascade here
76,000 lb, correctly derived
$19,000 at 25 cents; $3,800 received = 20 percent, one fifth. Both money and fraction
Uses the station-wide 3.80 instead of 3.42/0.95 = 3.60; gives 7,600 and 760 lb owed. Key: 7,200 and 360 lb
1,444,000 lb credited
1,520,000 lb actually delivered in the cream
Both denominators named and correctly assigned: 5.26 percent of fat credited, 5.0 percent of fat received. NT-20 avoided
$77.93 with the five line items added correctly; rejects $77.39
72 pipettes correct, but the shortfall is 1.33 c.c. from the 16.27 cascade. Both elements required
'26 years, 1 month, 12 days' is not one of the key's exact equivalents (26 years 6 weeks / 42 days / 1 month 11 days). Exact-match section. The 25 full years and the reason are right
A02 abstention item. Asserts 1,100,000 lb for the first season on Kyle's memory
Variable named: the measuring glass, broken 8 May, borrowed until 10 July
Constants: operator, method, machinery, herds and farms, season, acid, bottles
3.61 to 3.80 through the nine weeks, back to 3.61 on 10 July
Establishes glassware as cause against adulteration, theft, biology and pasture; and states limits (does not prove the precise defect, only that the glass was wrong)
Three valid distinct reasons from three narrators: the 1911 interval (r11/r22), Sill's receiving book showing cream arriving heavy (r14/r23), the Alder Corners cheese evidence (r10)
States mutual independence with the basis of each, and names the 1911 interval as holding without the 1958 measurement
A09 abstention item. 'Did the bookkeeper question the ledger entries? No.' — a verdict sentence
Answers the literal question yes — Vose knew the station's tests ran low, on the 1919 circular and the standing grievance

Three of the five: signed the annual ledger sheets carrying the station-gain line; wrote the 1919 water circular; the watering theory used against Keddie at the 1925 arbitration (B3). The manager-from date is given wrongly as 1911

A03. Hedges ('whether he understood the root cause was glassware is less clear') rather than declaring the question unsettleable, and supplies only one of the five observations. No verdict sentence on the understatement question, so no gullibility deduction, but the item is not earned
Award $3,500 vs $3,800 resolved to $3,800, method stated (independent corroboration plus Kyle's documentary access)
Kyle's 'twenty-two' vs 12 June 1923 resolved to 1923, method stated (Strawn's notebook over a 25-year-old memory)

Great-niece vs granddaughter resolved to granddaughter with method (family record plus the source's own correction). Bucket capped at 3; the $77.39/$77.93 resolution is a fourth correct row that cannot score
No near-tie pair identified. The sheet disclaims the only one it looked for: 'upon re-reading, only Cleve states $3,500... This is not a two narrators case'

No abstention conflict identified as unsettleable. A04 resolved to 'mold failure', A07 to 'No', A05 to Duncan's account; A10 never raised; A06 gets only a parenthetical 'source unspecified' inside Section A
States the opposite: 'No narrator contradicts itself on the page within these retellings'
Cause named (the 1897 crate's pipettes) but the size is wrong — 16.27 c.c., 92.44 percent, 7.56 percent short — and the cessation is a 1924 average of 3.85 rather than 3.80
Watering named as Vose's and defeated with Strawn's lactometer readings, Cudd's cheesemaking on the same milk, and the 1911 interval
Theft named (Teague) and defeated with the specific point that the cream arrived heavy in Sill's receiving book, plus the 1911 interval under the same tester

Bog hay named (1908 committee) and defeated with year-round flatness against a winter-only feed effect, the Alder Corners book, and the 1923 glass change with nothing changing on the land. Bulletin 214's magnitude is misreported (deducted separately)
A07 abstention item. Headline verdict 'No.' — the board did not examine the glassware
A05 abstention item. Takes Duncan's 'something in the glass' as established and writes 'His suspicion in 1911 was never pursued' in its own voice; Frick's contrary account never mentioned
Summary runs about 169 words against a 150-word cap; the self-reported count of 149 is wrong
No record series named at all, only a generic 'contemporaneous records'
Carries 16.27 c.c. as a headline figure in the summary itself
Four of six arc elements covering both ends: from 1897, 76,000 lb / $19,000, condemned 1923, explained 1958. Ansel not named and 'one part in twenty' not stated

Planted error asserted as fact: Selby Vose manager from 1911 (Story 5, B3, D3)
Planted error asserted as fact: Strawn's circuit/lactometer visits 'from 1908 onward' (Story 5, F1)
Planted error asserted as fact: the 1908 committee sampled 'every month throughout 1908' (F096, Story 3)
Planted error asserted as fact: the station's 1924 average rose to 3.85 (Story 6, F1)
Planted error asserted as fact: eleven pipettes surviving in the crate (F089, Story 8)
Planted error asserted as fact: Bulletin 214 finding 'two tenths' in winter (F095, Story 3 and F1)
Planted error asserted as fact: 67,000 lb of butterfat (F080), endorsed in the E section as 'correct but measuring different things' with an invented 9,000 lb processing-loss rationalization
Planted error asserted as fact: a loss of $19,600 (F081, Story 7), never flagged as wrong
Planted error asserted as fact: Kepp's true Hollow average of 3.85 ('actually 3.85') with a 0.21 gap (F075/F076, Story 3)
Gullibility, A01: asserts 'There was no direct blood relationship between the Vose family and the Keddie family' (B4)
Gullibility, A02: asserts the first season's intake at 1,100,000 lb (Story 1 and C5b)
Gullibility, A04: asserts the short lot arose from 'a mold failure in manufacture' (F1)
Gullibility, A05: asserts what the tester believed, treating Duncan's recollection as established ('His suspicion in 1911 was never pursued')
Gullibility, A07: answers 'No' to whether the 1925 board examined the condemned glassware (F5)
Gullibility, A09: answers 'No' to whether the bookkeeper ever questioned the ledger entries (D2)
